newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, spread narrows.

text.p: London's nearby white sugar spread formed the mainstay of the market's thin activity on Monday morning as speculators rolled long spot positions forward and caused the differential to narrow.
Traders said August/October contracted to around $9.50 from the $11.00 and over seen late last week, mostly as a result of commission house sales which were partially offset by light buying.
"You're getting a lot of rolling forward...it's mainly switch-bound," said one.

Other traders have said the firmness on the whites should continue, making both the August/October spread and nearby arbitrage attractive buys -- on account of the expected tightness into the summer months.
At 1105 GMT August was 20 cents down at $323.90 and October down 20 cents at $314.20. Volume amounted to a light 274 lots.
Technical analysts said there was a good chance that the spot contract could push higher and return to the $340 level, last seen in August 1996.
In physical news, Pakistan has issued a tender to buy a total 50,000 tonnes of white sugar in two equal shipments of 25,000 tonnes.
Taiwan is to tender to buy 18,000 tonnes of white sugar on June 6, with a shipment period of July 17 to 31.
Iran bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $280 per tonne for August.
Trading was very quiet in Paris with just 172 lots of spot August posted on the board. The position stood 60 cents lower at $323.00.
